summary.headline: Huhtamaki India Q1 FY26 EBITDA up 24.8% YoY on mix and efficiency; sales up only ~10 bps, EBIT hit by INR 88 mn prior-period depreciation charge.
summary.overview: Management reported sales broadly flat (up about 10 bps YoY) with EBITDA up 24.8% YoY, attributed to higher-value sales mix and operational efficiency. Reported EBIT was about INR 386 mn after a one-off INR 88 mn depreciation charge for prior two years (WDV instead of SLM error), with EBIT margin ex-charge at about 8% (27.8% EBIT margin ex-charge is stated in the call and appears to be an inconsistent figure relative to the 8% quoted). Reported PAT of about INR 256 crore was roughly 2% lower YoY; management said it rose about 23.1% excluding the prior-year charge. Raw material costs rose sharply from end-March on the Middle East conflict; management said most of the increase was passed through to customers, with low-to-medium double-digit RM impact.

financial_highlights.value: ~8% (sequential trend chart, excl. prior-period item); management also cited 27.8% ex-exceptional
financial_highlights.change: ~170 bps higher than Q1 last year on the 8% basis
~2% lower YoY; up ~23.1% excluding prior-year charge

financial_highlights.metric: Interest on income tax refund (other income)
financial_highlights.change: Other income roughly doubled YoY per analyst

financial_highlights.value: INR 106 crore vs INR 95 crore prior quarter
financial_highlights.change: QoQ increase; management said not substantial

segments.name: Flexible packaging (sole reported business)
segments.commentary: Growth focused on selected customers and higher-value categories (innovation, premiumisation, sustainability). Management said it is deliberately not participating in some low-value segments, which limits volume growth.

guidance_outlook: Management said raw-material cost increases are being passed through, so margin impact is expected to be minimal; top-line should rise mechanically from pass-through, barring market changes.
Management said the impact will be more visible in Q2 FY26 results, due end-July 2026.
No numerical guidance on growth or margins was given; management said it cannot disclose exact figures.
Solar captive power project at Khopoli is signed and in execution; expected to go live in the next few months, with benefits from H2.
Demand growth expected in line with industry norms: large FMCG customers 2-5%, smaller regional customers faster; industry growth cited at 6-7% per year by management.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation not disclosed; management said capacity is not a constraint and there is 'a lot of room to grow'.
Solar captive electricity project at Khopoli plant under execution, expected to go live within months.
Solvent consumption reduction: capital spent on solvent cooling and other equipment; all plants reducing solvent use.
Zero liquid discharge status at Khopoli, Rudrapur and Silvassa; plans to extend to other plants.
Property in Daman put up for sale after curtailing operations there.
demand_pricing: Raw material costs (films, paper) rose from end-March 2026 with volatility; management estimated low-to-medium double-digit RM impact on products overall, and said availability is not an issue.
Pricing: India was among the first regions to pass through costs; by end-March almost all future orders were locked at new prices, with contracts allowing pass-through.
Customers came with panic-driven volume requests during the conflict; management said demand has since stabilised with no significant change.
Competition: large multinational customers grow slowly; smaller regional Indian players grow faster. Management said it is not chasing low-value volume.
Analyst cited annual report reference to Indian flexible packaging growing 10-12%; management said the comparison is not like-for-like because the definition includes paper.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material cost impact post-war and is availability an issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices rose from end-March and are volatile; low-to-medium double-digit RM impact overall. Availability is not an issue given global procurement, though shipments from overseas can be delayed. Most costs passed to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments are seeing demand post-war and how is cost affecting demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers initially over-ordered in panic, then volumes stabilised. No significant demand change; large FMCG customers grow 2-5%, regional customers faster.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company losing share given the 10-12% market growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the market includes multinationals and smaller regional Indian players growing faster; the company is selective and focused on innovation and premium customers, so growth is in line with its value proposition. Amit Gupta said the market definition includes paper and is not comparable.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the jump in other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest on an income tax refund (about INR 6.5 crore), higher FD interest, and FX gains on exports from rupee weakness. Management said several one-offs offset this.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in other expenses from INR 95 crore to INR 106 crore QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase is not substantial, expense ratios are declining as a percentage of sales, and the one-offs include provision reversals and the INR 88 mn depreciation charge plus a property charge.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 100 crore ECB repayment to the parent extended from Feb 2026 to June 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: The ECB loan from the parent follows RBI tenure guidelines; part has been repaid and the balance is payable by June 2027. Servicing cost is linked to FD returns, so no negative impact, per management.

risks_watch: Q2 FY26 margin impact of raw material pass-through lag and volatility in RM prices, given the Middle East conflict.
Whether the INR 88 mn prior-period depreciation error is contained, and whether any further prior-period adjustments emerge.
Rising other expenses QoQ (INR 106 crore vs INR 95 crore) and reliance on non-operating income (interest and FX gains) in reported profit.
Volume growth weakness versus industry, as the company deprioritises lower-value customers.
Balance sheet: INR 100 crore parent ECB repayment deferred to June 2027; Daman property sale.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and pass-through execution, but evasive on quantitative items such as capacity utilisation, RM cost percentages and the other-expense increase, citing competitive sensitivity. New CFO Amit Gupta was more cautious in answering questions on drivers.
key_quotes: We are going after higher-value business, which is also consistent with our strategy and our strength in terms of the innovation leader in the industry.
We did an excellent job where we passed on most of these costs to our customers.
So capacity is not a constraint at the moment.
We have corrected the books of accounts, both from a P&L and the balance sheet standpoint and all the reflections in the P&L are coming correct starting from January 2026.
